Title: Best way to learn how to play?

Messages.Author: Chris Brightwell
Messages.Body:
I've played Magic: The Gathering casually with a few friends since
3rd Edition was out.

The other day, we found a sealed starter box of Jyhad cards at at
garage sale for $3, and bought it without hesitation. We've read through
the rulebook a few times, and grasp the basics of the game. I think.

My question is this -- is there an online tutorial or software
application designed to ease new players into the game? We don't know
*anyone* that plays, and can assume that one starter box will be able to
build two or three fairly decent decks.

Thanks for any help/ideas/thoughts/suggestions.

--
chris // cdb.webhop.org

For the current Set (Camarilla Edition) which can be considered a "basic"
set there are 5 Starters : Malkavian, Toreador, Nosferatu, Ventrue, Tremere.
These are all playable against each other and you can have quite some fun
with them. They can also mix with older Starters from Sabbat War Edition.

If you like the game and want to get more into it try to contact a local
prince (organisators in the worldwide V:EKN player network). There names and
emails can be found somewhere on http://www.white-wolf.com/VTES/

Messages.Author: Timlagor
Messages.Body:



No one really seems to have registered that you already have this box.
I reckon a whole box of Jyhad boosters ought to build you a few decks.
VTES is kinda weird from that point of view in that you suddenly go
from not being able to build anything decent to being able to build
almost anything. That's why they produced the preconstructed clan
decks. Certainly you have enough cards to give the game a good bash
and see if you like it.

If you each read the rules you'll probably be able to play ok
-especially if you have done the demo. It might go quite slowly at
first.

I recommend sorting your cards by Disciplines and Clans. IF you have
12 Vamps of some clans make them your crypt -then take all the cards
using their clan disciplines and split the cards that don't need a
Discipline or Clan to play. Then PLAY the game. I wouldn't worry too
much about deck construction or who wins or anything initially -just
see what comes up and how it works -then you'll be able to think about
it properly. (of course this may be appalling advice or you may
already know the cards quite well by the time you read this ;-)
My other bit of advice is do your deck building when you have no one
to play with rather than spending time you could be playing in ;-)

Have fun! :-)
